Apply PHW styling to a flextable

Source: R/flextable.R
phw_flextable_theme.Rd

Styles an existing flextable the way PHW and its Communicable Disease Surveillance Centre (CDSC) present tables in reports. Four styles are available:

Usage

phw_flextable_theme(
  x,
  style = c("booktabs", "header", "light", "zebra"),
  font_size = 10,
  font_family = phw_font(),
  bold_first_col = FALSE,
  total_row = FALSE,
  accent = phw_colours[["navy"]],
  header_bg = NULL,
  header_colour = NULL,
  text_colour = phw_colours[["text"]],
  stripe_colour = phw_colours[["grey_bg"]],
  padding = c(3, 5),
  align = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A flextable.

style

"booktabs", "header", "light" or "zebra".

font_size

Body font size in points. Header uses the same size.

font_family

Font family.

bold_first_col

Bold the first column? (Area names in many PHW tables.)

total_row

Treat the last row as a total row (bold with a rule above)?

accent

Colour of the rules and header (navy by default).

header_bg, header_colour

Override the header fill and text colour.

text_colour

Body text colour.

stripe_colour

Fill for alternate rows in "zebra".

padding

Cell padding in points: one number, or c(top_bottom, left_right), or NULL to keep the existing padding (for tables that use padding for indents, such as gtsummary output).

align

Align numbers right and text left automatically? Set to FALSE to keep your own alignment.

Value

A flextable.

Details

  • "booktabs" (default): horizontal rules only, as in printed journal tables: a navy rule above and below the header and along the bottom, a bold header, no vertical lines and no fill.

  • "header": a navy header band with white bold text.

  • "light": a light-teal header band with dark text (as in the weekly acute respiratory infection report).

  • "zebra": "booktabs" plus light grey banding on alternate rows.

Numbers are right-aligned and text is left-aligned. In every style the font is Ubuntu (or the phw_font() fallback).

Examples

if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ft <- flextable::flextable(head(airquality))
  phw_flextable_theme(ft)
}
